about.title: Beaumont Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Beaumont recorded 4 traffic deaths alongside 86 injury collisions in the most recent final crash year, numbers that translate into real families across Riverside County now facing life without someone they loved. When a death results from a crash on I-10, Oak Valley Parkway, 6th Street, or anywhere else in town, California law allows certain surviving family members to pursue a civil wrongful death claim separate from any criminal proceeding. That claim can address funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the family depended on, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance the person provided. Standing to file is limited by law, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and there is a strict two-year deadline from the date of death, shorter if a government entity is involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving Beaumont families with an independent attorney who can explain options clearly and handle the legal work on contingency, so there's nothing owed unless money is recovered.

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then other dependents or heirs. An independent attorney can review your relationship to the deceased and explain where you fit.

items.title: Racing Against a Strict Clock
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, and that window shrinks significantly when a government entity is involved. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the LawProactive network work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and nothing owed unless a recovery happens. That structure lets families focus on grieving instead of legal bills.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify to step forward. An independent attorney can look at your specific family situation and clarify exactly where you stand.

items.question: Is a wrongful death case connected to any criminal charges from the crash?
items.answer: No, a wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that might arise from the same crash. The civil case focuses on financial and personal losses to the family, while criminal proceedings, if any, are handled independently by prosecutors.

items.question: Does it matter that our crash happened near a busy Beaumont corridor like I-10 or Oak Valley Parkway?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't change your legal rights, but documenting exactly where and how the crash occurred, including nearby Beaumont roads, still matters for building the claim. An independent attorney can gather police reports and public collision records tied to that specific stretch of road as part of the case.

items.question: What kinds of losses can a wrongful death claim actually cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses typically include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, so an independent attorney can walk through what applies to your circumstances.
